title: SEO Starter Guide: The Basics | Google Search Central  |  Documentation  |  Google for Developers

facts.fact: Changes made to a website can take anywhere from a few hours to several months to be reflected on Google's end.
facts.value: a few hours to several months
facts.quote: Some changes might take effect in a few hours, others could take several months.

facts.fact: Google's guide says you should generally wait a few weeks to assess whether your work had beneficial effects in Google Search results.
facts.quote: In general, you likely want to wait a few weeks to assess whether your work had beneficial effects in Google Search results.

facts.fact: Google's crawler, when checking location-dependent page content, generally operates from the US, so that is the location whose view of the information matters.
facts.quote: make sure you're satisfied with the information that Google sees from its crawler's location, which is generally the US.

facts.fact: Google says using directories to group similar pages can affect how it crawls and indexes a site once the site has more than a few thousand URLs.
facts.quote: If you have more than a few thousand URLs on your site, how you organize your content may have effects on how Google crawls and indexes your site.

facts.fact: Google states that sites following the Search Essentials are more likely to show up in Google's search results, though no site is guaranteed inclusion in the index.
facts.quote: sites that follow the Search Essentials are more likely to show up in Google's search results

facts.fact: Having duplicate content on a site is not a violation of Google's spam policies, but it can be a bad user experience and search engines might waste crawling resources.
facts.quote: Having duplicate content on your site is not a violation of our spam policies, but it can be a bad user experience and search engines might waste crawling resources

facts.fact: Google says the vast majority of new pages it finds every day are discovered through links.
facts.quote: the vast majority of the new pages Google finds every day are through links

facts.fact: Google states that a site's content can influence its search presence more than any other suggestion in the guide.
facts.quote: Creating content that people find compelling and useful will likely influence your website's presence in search results more than any of the other suggestions in this guide

facts.fact: Google recommends that user-generated links on a site, such as forum posts or comments, have a nofollow or similar annotation automatically added by the CMS.
facts.quote: make sure every link that's posted by users has a `nofollow` or similar annotation automatically added by your CMS

facts.fact: Google says a good meta description is short, unique to one particular page, and includes the most relevant points of the page, typically one or two sentences.
facts.quote: which is typically a succinct, one- or two-sentence summary of the page

facts.fact: Google says search engines' language matching systems can understand how a page relates to many queries even without exact terms in them.
facts.quote: Google's language matching systems are sophisticated and can understand how your page relates to many queries, even if you don't explicitly use the exact terms in them

facts.fact: Google Search doesn't use the keywords meta tag.
facts.quote: doesn't use the keywords meta tag

facts.fact: Keyword stuffing, meaning excessively repeating the same words even in variations, is against Google's spam policies.
facts.quote: keyword stuffing is against Google's spam policies

facts.fact: Keywords in the domain name or URL path have hardly any ranking effect beyond appearing in breadcrumbs, according to Google.
facts.quote: the keywords in the name of the domain (or URL path) alone have hardly any effect beyond appearing in

facts.fact: According to Google, a domain's TLD only matters if you are targeting a specific country's users, and even then it is usually a low impact signal.
facts.quote: only matters if you're targeting a specific country's users, and even then it's usually a low impact signal

facts.fact: Google states there is no magical word count target for content, minimum or maximum, for ranking purposes.
facts.quote: there's no magical word count target, minimum or maximum

facts.fact: Google states that content under multiple URLs is fine and does not cause a manual action, though it is inefficient.
facts.quote: It's inefficient, but it's not something that will cause a manual action.

facts.fact: Google states that PageRank, which uses links, is only one of many ranking signals in Google Search.
facts.quote: We have many ranking signals, and PageRank is just one of those.

facts.fact: Google states that the order of headings does not matter from a Google Search perspective, and there is no ideal number of headings for a page.
facts.quote: it doesn't matter if you're using them out of order

facts.fact: Google states that E-E-A-T is not a ranking factor.
facts.quote: No, it's not.

facts.fact: Google describes alt text as added to HTML with the alt attribute of the img element, or through a CMS description field when uploading an image.
facts.quote: You can add this to your HTML with the `alt` attribute of the `img` element

facts.fact: Google recommends using images that are sharp and clear and placing them near text relevant to the image.
facts.quote: Use images that are sharp and clear, and place them near text that's relevant to the image.

facts.fact: Google describes word of mouth, where people familiar with a site tell friends about it, as one of the most effective and lasting ways to promote a site, though it can take time.
facts.quote: is word of mouth: that is, people familiar with your site tell their friends about it

facts.fact: Google warns that overpromoting a site can harm it, because people may get fatigued and search engines may perceive some practices as manipulation of search results.
facts.quote: you can overdo promoting your site and actually harm it

facts.fact: The Google Search Central YouTube channel contains hundreds of videos created for website owners, according to Google.
facts.quote: Watch hundreds of helpful videos created for website owners.
